outcome: CONTINUATION_INVALID stops being a bucket: every exit that produces it carries a stable machine-readable site label into the contract error detail and the journal, so the journal alone answers which mechanism fired.

exclude: renaming any error code recorded in existing journals

acceptance.text: Every fail("CONTINUATION_INVALID") site in the driver (responses, chat, continuation ledger) is replaced by a labelled constructor naming a stable site identifier (for example continuation.toolcall_decode.correlate_reuse), and a test enumerates the sites and asserts no unlabelled constructor remains.
The compound tool-call decode check at the site diagnosed in sworn#187 (eight conditions collapsed into one refusal, including correlate-on-replay) is split so each condition carries its own label.

The site label travels into the journal effect's error detail without renaming error_code, proven by a test that provokes a labelled refusal through a dispatch and reads the label back from the journal.
The three mechanisms already confirmed for the bucket - budget exhaustion, unrecognised vendor dialect, tool-call decode refusal - map to three distinct labels, pinned by unit tests.

constraints: error_code values are durable identifiers in existing journals: labels are additive detail, never a rename.

Evidence basis: sworn#187 - three unrelated faults surfaced as one opaque string across two releases; the operational diag build (runtime.Caller stderr labels) is the proof of value and is retired by this slice.
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
